Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

apply verb

put to use (a rule, a remedy)

also apply a rule, apply a remedy, put into practice

classical

Cic. Off. 1.134: sī sēriīs, sevēritātem adhibeat, sī jocōsīs, lepōrem
Traupman 62, 272, 370: remedium adhibēre

adhibeō, adhibēre, adhibuī, adhibitum

verb, second conjugation; with ad or in and the accusative, or the dative

apply, bring to bear, use

Lewis & Short: “to put a thing to a determinate use, to apply, to use or employ”, with intention, unlike ūtī. That a rule applies to someone is ad aliquem pertinet (see concern).

Other words

  • accommodō, accommodāre, accommodāvī, accommodātum — adapt, fit (to a case)

    verb, first conjugation; with ad and the accusative, or the dative · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 9.7 (Lewis & Short): meum cōnsilium accommodābō ad tuum

  • applicō, applicāre — attach, put against

    verb, first conjugation · avoid · classical · Cic. Amic. 81: ad quās sē applicent

    Classically to put one thing against another, or with sē to attach oneself to someone; not to apply a rule.

Examples

  • sī sēriīs, sevēritātem adhibeat, sī jocōsīs, lepōrem

    To serious things let him bring gravity, to playful things charm.Cic. Off. 1.134

  • habenda ratiō valētūdinis, ūtendum exercitātiōnibus modicīs, tantum cibī et pōtiōnis adhibendum ut reficiantur vīrēs, nōn opprimantur

    We must look after our health, take moderate exercise, and take just enough food and drink to restore our strength, not to crush it.Cic. Sen. 36

  • quod etiam rūsticīs nōtum est, quī frondibus tenerīs nōn putant adhibendam esse falcem

    Even countrymen know this: they do not think the pruning-knife should be put to tender shoots.Quint. 2.4.11

  • remedium adhibēre

    to apply a remedyTraupman 370

See also concern.
